sections.h2: Stark County Recorder: address and hours
sections.html:
The Stark County Recorder is on the first floor of the County Office Building at 110 Central Plaza South, Suite 170, Canton, OH 44702. The window is open 8:30 to 4:30 on weekdays, with no weekend hours. The office keeps the permanent record of deeds, mortgages and easements for all land in the county, and those records are searchable on its website around the clock at no direct cost to users.

Stark County has 374,853 residents and covers 581 square miles in northeastern Ohio. Canton is the county seat, and the other cities are Alliance, Canal Fulton, Louisville, Massillon and North Canton.

Not every record sits here. Birth and death requests go to the Stark County Health Department at 330-493-9904, marriage licenses to the Probate Court at 330-451-7755 and divorce records to the Family Court at 330-451-7415.

sections.h2: What does the Stark County Recorder charge?
sections.html:
The office does not set its own prices. The Ohio Revised Code does, in section 317.32. The printed schedule lists $34 for a deed's first two pages and $8 for each more, with $4 for each cross reference. The statute also lets counties add a small preservation charge, so call the Canton office to confirm the total before you mail a check.

Stark County Recorder price list
Document or serviceCharge
Deed or mortgage, first two pages$34.00
Every added page$8.00
Cross reference to an earlier document$4.00
Document that fails standardization rules$20.00
Health care power of attorney or living will$34.00
Staff-made copy, per page$2.00

Pay by cash, check, money order or card. Cards carry a 2.75 percent convenience fee. Checks go to the Stark County Recorder, and altered checks are refused. A page-count chart on the fee page tabulates totals up to 90 pages.

The Auditor's real estate transfer department must endorse the deed before the Recorder will take it. A deed cannot be recorded until it carries the Auditor's stamp showing the conveyance form was filed correctly under Revised Code 319.202. The transfer line is 330-451-7333, with a second number at 330-451-7322.

  • Form DTE 100 states the value on a taxable sale, and DTE 100 (EX) states why a transfer is exempt.
  • Property already receiving the homestead or owner-occupied reduction adds its own statement of conveyance.
  • The conveyance charge is $.004 of the price rounded up to the next hundred dollars, plus fifty cents per tax parcel.
  • Payment at that counter is by check or cash only.

The Auditor recommends that an attorney prepare the deed, though owners may draft their own. Either way, the deed needs the items in the next section.

sections.h2: What belongs on a Stark County deed?
sections.html:
A deed has to carry:

  • The grantor's marital status, which supports the release of dower rights.
  • The grantee's name and the tax parcel numbers.
  • A current legal description that follows the county's conveyance standards.
  • A reference to the prior deed instrument.
  • The signature of the grantor and of the grantor's spouse if married, whether or not the spouse is on the title.
  • A completed notary clause with the notary's signature.

Accepted deed types include administrator's, commissioner's, executor's, fiduciary, limited and special warranty, quit claim, sheriff's, survivorship, trustee and general warranty deeds. A sheriff's deed needs a description approval form, and a probate transfer arrives as a certificate of transfer or a judgment entry. A transfer on death designation affidavit, unlike most affidavits, does not require a certified death certificate.

sections.h2: Splits, combinations and the tax map office
sections.html:
Combinations and splits require a visit to the tax map office before the transfer. The Auditor offers a New Legal Description Application, a Tax Combine and Un-Combine Request and a Condominium Requirements checklist, and a sheriff's deed needs its own description approval form.

A seller of part of a lot or a corner of a farm should call the Auditor's maps line at 330-451-7341 before a closing is scheduled, because a deed cannot be recorded until the Auditor has stamped it. The office no longer asks for a stamped copy of the previous deed, but the new document must cite it.

Besides deeds and mortgages, the fee schedule prices a list of filings that can touch a house sale. Title searchers look for these, and a seller with an unpaid lien should expect a payoff request at closing.

  • Federal tax liens and Department of Justice liens, each with a separate release filing.
  • Abstracts of judgment, priced at five dollars.
  • State employment and workers' compensation liens, where the filing itself carries no fee.
  • UCC filings, priced per document and per name indexed.
  • Plats, priced by the square inch on the printed sizes of 11 by 17 up to 24 by 36.

Cross references at $4.00 each link a new document to an earlier recorded one.

sections.h2: Can I record or look up deeds online?
sections.html:
Documents may be recorded electronically through the E-Recording link on the Recorder's website, and anyone can search the records free. Ohio law pushed this along: ORC 317.13 requires every recorder to offer e-recording of conveyances and to put indexes and images online for instruments recorded since 1980.

Copies cost nothing online. In the office, a self-serve copy is ten cents a page, and a staff-assisted copy is $2.00 a page. To get a certified copy by mail, send the Recorder a written request, the fee and a stamped self-addressed envelope.

sections.h2: Getting a deed from signing to the record
sections.html:
A typical sale follows four stages. The seller signs before a notary, and the title company or attorney checks the legal description against the prior deed. The deed goes to the Auditor's transfer desk with the DTE form and the conveyance fee, by check or cash. The stamped deed then goes to the Recorder with the recording fee. Finally, the Recorder files it and it becomes searchable on the website.

If you are handling the paperwork without a title company, call both offices first. Confirm the current total, bring the prior deed number and notary details, and for a split or combination, visit the tax map office before anything else. A mismatch in the description or a missing spouse signature is the usual reason a deed is sent back. Sellers who have a lien on the property should ask the title company to find it early, since a payoff or release has to be recorded before the new owner's title is clean.

faqs.q: What is the Stark County Recorder's address?
faqs.a: Suite 170 at 110 Central Plaza South, Canton, OH 44702, on the first floor of the County Office Building. Hours run 8:30 to 4:30 on weekdays.

faqs.q: Is the Stark County recording fee really $34?
faqs.a: That is the printed amount for a deed's first two pages, with $8 for each added page. State law allows a surcharge of up to $5 per document, so ask the office to confirm the total before mailing.

faqs.q: Do I need the Auditor's stamp before recording in Stark County?
faqs.a: Yes. Recording waits for the Auditor's stamp, which shows the conveyance form was completed correctly. The Auditor accepts only a check or cash for the conveyance fee.

faqs.q: Can the Stark County Recorder take credit cards?
faqs.a: Yes, with a 2.75 percent convenience fee added. Cash, checks and money orders are also accepted, and checks should name the Stark County Recorder.

faqs.q: How do I get a certified copy of a recorded deed in Stark County?
faqs.a: Ask in person or mail a written request, the fee and a stamped self-addressed envelope. Staff-made copies are $2.00 a page, plus $1.00 to certify each document.
